title: Predictive analysis: what is likely to happen

videos.script: Otávio, the CFO, wants one number. How much will Varanda sell from January to March? {{question}} He needs it for the bank and for the stock orders. Lívia gives him a number and a range, and this lesson is about why the range matters more. {{methods}} You start with three methods anybody can run in a spreadsheet. Repeat last month. Repeat the same month last year. Or repeat last year, adjusted for how fast the company is growing. {{backtest}} Then you test them on the past. You pretend it is June 2025, forecast the rest of the year, and compare each forecast with what really happened. One method misses by sixteen per cent. The best misses by about two, except in October. {{error}} You measure the misses, check which way they lean, and turn the typical one into a range for 2026. {{fail}} Last, the places where any forecast breaks: something new, a sudden change, and a forecast that changes the very thing it predicts.
